study type: Secondary analysis of a double-blind, single-center, randomized controlled trial
outcome: Composite severe neonatal morbidity and mortality
cohort: 955 nulliparous patients with singleton pregnancies at 36 weeks of gestation or later who presented in spontaneous labor and received oxytocin for labor augmentation
finding: In multivariable analyses, there were no significant differences in maternal or perinatal adverse outcomes based on exceeding 20 milliunits/min of oxytocin.
mod_finding: Maximum oxytocin dose rates greater than 20 milliunits/min were not significantly associated with cesarean delivery rates.
